note: The ISA comparison at constant DIE POWER, 27 Aug 2026 -- the experiment the registered prediction should have specified. scripts/isa_constant_power.sh, 24 points attempted.
why: The constant-DENSITY sweep let a smaller die dissipate less power, so it came out cooler and flatter and the prediction was falsified against a confound rather than against physics. Holding total watts fixed makes the compaction real.
RESULT: HALF THE SWEEP HAS NO STEADY STATE. At constant power the two most compact dies -- arm_n2 (48.4 mm^2) and riscv_p670 (38.6 mm^2) -- diverge at BOTH power levels, including 25 W where their densities are only 0.517 and 0.648 W/mm^2, comfortably under the 0.80-0.85 W/mm^2 grease cliff measured on the x86 die.
why_they_fail_below_the_x86_cliff: Because the cliff is not a property of density alone. A compact die is penalised TWICE. Its power density is higher at the same watts -- 2.1x for arm_n2 -- and the spreading boundary it sees is WORSE, because that boundary scales with die area (docs/evidence/spreading_boundary_by_die.json: 0.553 K/W on the 53 mm^2 die against 0.325 on the 101 mm^2 one and 0.108 on the 826 mm^2 GA100). Roughly 2.1x the density into roughly 1.8x the boundary resistance is about 3.7x the temperature rise, which is why they run away.
the_honest_reading: This is a statement about COMPACTION AT A FIXED COOLER, which is as much a packaging result as an architecture one. It does NOT say ARM or RISC-V cores are thermally unviable -- a real compact part would be cooled differently, and the area-dependent boundary is the term that would change. What it does say is that at constant power, shrinking the die is thermally expensive in a way that density alone does not capture, and that any ISA comparison holding watts fixed has to model the cooler per die area or it is measuring the wrong thing.
taken_with_the_constant_density_sweep: The two together bracket the answer. At constant DENSITY a compact die is cooler, flatter and MORE expensive to cool per kelvin of margin (isa_benefit_prediction_test.json). At constant POWER it has no steady state at all. Neither supports the original prediction that compact cores are better MR targets, and they fail it for different reasons -- which is worth more than a single falsification.
